title: How to surpass no-go limits in Gaussian quantum error correction and entangled Gaussian state distillation

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says: 'In general, \tilde{M}_i is not symplectic since Z_i is not symplectic.' This implication is invalid: for a symplectic M, \tilde{M}_i = Z_i M Z_i is symplectic because (Z_i M Z_i)^T \Omega (Z_i M Z_i) = \Omega, since Z_i^T \Omega Z_i = -\Omega and M^T \Omega M = \Omega. In the present protocol M is a symplectic Gaussian unitary (beam splitter/squeezer), so the asserted non-symplectic character is wrong.

Equation (13) writes the partial-transposed covariance evolution as Z_i M Z_i \gamma(\rho) Z_i M Z_i + Z_i N Z_i. But for a Gaussian channel G^{M,N}, covariance evolves as \gamma \mapsto M \gamma M^T + N. With \tilde{M}_i = Z_i M Z_i and \tilde{N}_i = Z_i N Z_i, the correct expression is Z_i M Z_i \gamma Z_i M^T Z_i + Z_i N Z_i; the right-hand factor must be transposed unless M is symmetric.

The proof writes \mathcal{G}_{1,2}^{I,\sigma^2 B_2^2 S(-r)S^T(-r)B_2^T} and then \mathcal{G}_{1,2}^{I,\sigma^2 Z_2^2 B_2 Z_2^2 S(-r)S^T(-r) Z_2 B_2^T Z_2}. These expressions are internally inconsistent and do not match the correct expression used in Appendix F, namely \sigma^2 Z_2 B Z_2 S(-r)S^T(-r)Z_2 B^T Z_2. The extra squares/inconsistent Z_2 factors would not give the claimed N^{polar}.

The paper states that concatenation is useful when 4/\ln(\pi^{1.5}/(2\sigma^4)) + 1 < e^{4r}. Comparing Eq. (16) with Eq. (15) gives a different condition: with L = \ln(\pi^{1.5}/(2\sigma^4)), benefit requires e^{-2r}\sqrt{L+4r} < L, i.e. e^{4r} > (L+4r)/L^2, not 1+4/L < e^{4r}. Thus Eq. (17) is not the correct usefulness condition from the displayed formulas.

The text states '\sigma^2 < \frac{\pi^{3}}{4\sqrt{2e}} \approx 1.012'. But \pi^3/(4\sqrt{2e}) \approx 31.006/9.324 \approx 3.33, not 1.012. The approximate value 1.012 corresponds instead to an expression such as \pi^{3/4}/\sqrt{2e}, so the printed formula is numerically wrong.

Appendix B writes \hat{D}_j(\alpha) = e^{i\sqrt{2}(\mathrm{Im}\{\alpha\}\hat{q}_j + \mathrm{Re}\{\alpha\}\hat{p}_j)}. From the main text definition \hat{D}(\alpha)=e^{\alpha\hat{a}^\dagger-\alpha^*\hat{a}}, the correct expression is e^{i\sqrt{2}(\mathrm{Im}\{\alpha\}\hat{q} - \mathrm{Re}\{\alpha\}\hat{p})}, so the sign of the p-term is wrong in Appendix B and in the same convention used in Appendix C.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A, after Eq. (A4), displacement transpose identity
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text claims '\hat{D}^T(\alpha) = (\hat{D}^\dagger(\alpha))^* = \hat{D}(-\alpha^*)'. The final equality for D^T(\alpha) is correct, but the intermediate equality is false: (\hat{D}^\dagger(\alpha))^* = \hat{D}(\alpha), not \hat{D}(-\alpha^*), because complex conjugation of a displacement operator gives \hat{D}(\beta)^* = \hat{D}(-\beta).
